title: A view model
description:
Write the view model behind a tip calculator window. It never touches a window, so it can be tested like any class:

```csharp
public abstract class ViewModelBase : INotifyPropertyChanged
public sealed class RelayCommand(Action execute, Func<bool> canExecute) : ICommand    // with NotifyCanExecuteChanged()

public sealed class TipViewModel : ViewModelBase
{
    public string BillText { get; set; }     // what the user typed, "" at the start
    public int TipPercent { get; set; }      // 15 at the start, kept between 0 and 30
    public int People { get; set; }          // 1 at the start, kept at 1 or more
    public string Total { get; }             // e.g. "57.50", or "" when the bill is not valid
    public string PerPerson { get; }         // the total divided between people, or ""
    public string Error { get; }             // "Enter the bill amount" when BillText is not a positive number, else ""
    public RelayCommand AddPersonCommand { get; }
    public RelayCommand RemovePersonCommand { get; }   // can execute only while People > 1
    public RelayCommand ResetCommand { get; }          // back to "", 15, 1
}
```

- The bill is parsed with the invariant culture. Total = bill × (1 + tip / 100) and per person = total / people, both rounded to cents (halves away from zero) and shown with 2 decimals.
- Setting a property to the value it already has raises **nothing**. Otherwise `PropertyChanged` is raised for the property itself and then for every computed property that depends on it (`Total`, `PerPerson`, `Error`), in that order. Values outside the allowed range are clamped first.
- When `People` changes, `RemovePersonCommand` raises `CanExecuteChanged`.
hints: A protected `Set(ref field, value)` in the base class does the "compare, assign, raise" work once; each setter then only adds what depends on it.
`RemovePersonCommand` must tell the view to ask `CanExecute` again whenever `People` changes: call its `NotifyCanExecuteChanged()` in the `People` setter.
